answer: Each identity earns standing by transcribing 40 unique 5-minute harbour recordings assigned by its key hash — waves on a jetty, voices on a terrace, static shaped like a nebula in the spectrogram. Verifiers score it against hidden ground truth; below 95% accuracy the slot is refused and work is discarded. One set takes about 9 focused hours and cannot be copied, since every recording differs. Scaling to 1,000 Sybils means 9,000 hours of distinct listening, paying real labour per fake with no batch shortcut. Trade-off: deaf-accessible alternatives are needed and slow typists are disadvantaged.
